title: Gateway bifurcation for graceful multi-region takeover with per-connection KV checkpointing
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: During regional disruptions we currently perform blunt traffic drains or full cutovers that can truncate long-lived streaming sessions and lose in-flight KV state. This causes visible client disconnects, token replays, and SLO violations for tail latency and availability.

Goal: Implement a gateway bifurcation pattern that enables graceful takeover between two active regions that share a coordinated per-connection KV checkpointing mechanism, short token-grace window, and circuit-decay policy. The mechanism should: preserve active streaming attachments where possible, reduce user-visible interruptions, maintain SLOs for p95/p99 latency, and allow progressive traffic rebalancing with automated load-shedding triggers and circuit breakers for overloaded endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: New gateway bifurcation control plane can execute staged traffic split 100% -> 80/20 -> 50/50 -> 0% with per-connection checkpointing applied during each stage
Active streaming sessions can resume on target region with KV checkpoint replay within token-grace window for >= 95% of test sessions in canary
Circuit-decay policy triggers and drops low-priority background requests while preserving high-priority tokens; measured p99 latency remains within SLO (<= 800ms) during 70% simulated surge
Automated rollback when telemetry shows error-rate delta > 2% or SLA budget burn > 30% in 10m window
End-to-end observability: dashboards for per-connection handoff success rate, checkpoint latency, token-grace expirations, and circuit-breaker activations are available in Console
Runbook updated with step-by-step operator commands and emergency cutover procedure
design_notes: Bifurcation model: introduce a light-weight control plane API that instructs edge gateways to enter a 'bifurcate' mode where connections are tracked and checkpoints emitted at defined safe boundaries (e.g., sentence boundaries or invocation end for non-streams)
KV checkpointing uses existing prefix cache format but augments with 'handoff-metadata' containing sequence id and minimal opaque resume token
Token-grace window: short TTL (default 45s) during which requests with valid resume token are allowed on destination region before full auth revalidation, configurable per-customer
Circuit-decay: instead of hard reject on threshold breach, reduce priority of non-interactive routes progressively using weighted drop and backoff so that interactive sessions retain headroom
We will avoid synchronous cross-region KV replication; instead use per-connection snapshot + opportunistic async pre-warm on destination to keep overhead low
technical_approach: Edge changes: gateway will emit checkpoint artifacts to S3-backed artifact store (or internal blob cache) keyed by connection-id and region, with signed short-lived pointer visible to target region

Control plane: bifurcate controller service with APIs: /start-bifurcate, /advance-stage, /rollback, /finalize. Controller computes staged percentages and pushes policies to gateways via gRPC config streams

Resume flow: destination gateway receives resume token, fetches checkpoint, rehydrates KV cache and replay last few tokens to restore deterministic decoder state; if checkpoint unavailable or stale, fallback to canonical stateless retry path
Load-shedding triggers: telemetry-driven rules based on queue depth, GPU headroom, and p99 latency; rules feed into controller which adjusts split and activates circuit-decay rules
Safety nets: global circuit-breaker per-customer that can instant-fail new sessions to protect cluster and prevent cascading failures
Backwards compatibility: non-streaming and stateless flows unaffected; default behavior for customers not opted-in remains original cutover path
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Internal Canary: deploy bifurcate controller and edge code to test cluster; run synthetic suite with deterministic streams (2/10 - 2/24)
Phase 1 - Limited Canary: enable feature for internal services only, monitor handoff success and token-grace expirations, iterate on checkpoint size and pre-warm thresholds (3/1 - 3/8)
Phase 2 - Customer Canary: opt-in 3 low-risk customers with long-lived streams; run staged splits with progressive % increases (3/9 - 3/16)
Phase 3 - Ramp: enable auto-split for broad traffic with conservative defaults and telemetry thresholds; maintain human-in-loop for first 48 hours (3/17 - 3/24)
Rollback: emergency commands in runbook to abort and redirect all bifurcate traffic back to original region and invalidate resume tokens
telemetry: Per-connection metrics: checkpoint_size_bytes, checkpoint_emit_latency_ms, resume_fetch_latency_ms, resume_success_bool
SLOs: p95/p99 latency pre/post-handshake, availability per-region, error-rate by route
Alerting: conservative alerts for handoff_success_rate < 90% in 5m and p99 latency regression > 20% vs baseline
test_plan: Automated unit tests for checkpoint serialization/deserialization and token signing
Integration tests with simulated cross-region resume using local artifact store
Chaos tests: introduce network partitions and verify controller rolling advance/rollback semantics
Load tests: synthetic streams plus background embedding/ingest traffic to evaluate circuit-decay efficacy
Canary dashboards and SLIs tracked during each stage; automatic gates for phase transition
risks: Resume token leakage: mitigated by short TTLs and signature verification; requires security review
Large checkpoints may add storage/IO pressure during mass handoffs; mitigation: cap checkpoint size and prefer incremental diffs
Checkpoint replay may diverge for non-deterministic model serving paths (e.g., sampling); mitigation: restrict replay to deterministic sampling or force deterministic mode during handoff windows
Increased control plane complexity and blast radius if controller miscomputes split — mitigations: rate limits, circuit-breakers, and manual abort
SLO trade-off: during surge the system may favor availability of interactive sessions by dropping background work; this needs clear product communication
